kabul Killings

By: Diana Lucas | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Devastated as news of the death of South African family killed in Kabul

Summary:
Kabul Killing
Werner Groenewald, 46, his son, Jean-Pierre, 17, and daughter, Rodé, 15, were killed in Saturday’s attack at their Kabul home on the compound of Partnership in Academics and Development. Werner’s wife, Hannelie, a doctor, was working at a hospital when the attack began.
We speak to Riana du Plessis, Hannelie’s sister “It was their life mission, to train the Afghans, to support them, to help them.”
She said the attack had apparently been carried out by three people dressed as policemen, including a suicide bomber.
Du Plessis said: “The Taliban thought that they [the South Africans} were trying to convert Muslims to be Christians. They targeted my brother-in-law, Werner.” .
He and his children had been taken aside and shot and they bled to death, she said.
We look at the situation in Kabul, possible reasons why the family were killed. We talk to Dutch Reformed Church in Moreleta Park in Pretoria, where Groenewald had been a full-time pastor.
The Dominee Willem Badenhorst said the family had been in Kabul to serve the community.

Press Release:


Kabul Killings
Confusion has clouded media reports around the killing of three members of the Groenewald family in Kabul this week. Survivor and mother Hannelie Groenewald, still in Afghanistan, has communicated to her sister Riana Du Plessis the truth of what happened when her husband and two teenagers were shot dead by militants. Carte Blanche reports on a family's choice to live among the Afghan people.


Script:


Link
Last Saturday, South African Werner Groenwald and his two children were shot dead in their house in Kabul… Afghanistan. Hanelie Werner’s wife escaped the same fate because she had been called out to the hospital where she worked as a doctor.

V/O 8 sec
It was Riana du Plessis, Hannelie’s sister, who first heard heard the tragic news, when Hannelie phoned her that evening.

Riana: When Hanelie talked to me she was very calm but I was horrified, I was in shock and immediately started screaming.

V/O 11 sec
Werner, Riana’s brother in law was working for an ngo, teaching agriculture and building schools. Hannelie. a Dr, worked at a local hospital ….

Riana : Werner and the kids were like normal South frican family very happy in Afghanistan they loved the country and they loved their lives there. When I asked them when were they coming back they said to me they said to me their lives are in Afghanistan.

V/O 8 sec
They had been living in Kabul for 12 years and their two children Jean Pierre and Rode were more Afghan than South African.

Devi: You were their aunt tell me about those children?
Riana: I was very close to those kids, I can tell you I had communication with those kids every day. Rode was I want to say the more, every morning she would sms me it was the funniest thing I woke up and got this sms Helo, she was Rode she was a very smart kid. Jean Pierre the softer one, helpful one, Rode was totally different.

V/0 6 sec
And they might have been totally integrated in life there, there was always a touch of home…

Riana: Hannelie had parties and you weren’t believe it, they introduced braai vleis to Americans, the Australians, the British. Hannelie liked baking the cakes she baked specific cakes with a specific theme.

Pastor Dirkie van der Spuy: We loved them so much he was a very soft spoken man, friendly he didn’t have any enemies.

V/O 10 sec
Pastor Dirkie van der Spuy has known the family for 20 years, the Groenewalds were members of the Dutch Reformed Church, Morelete Park in Pretoria.


Dirkie:: It’s a heart breaking thing he died for doing good to people. A war stricken place a where everything is broken and been shot down to the ground he decided to do more than say shame I hope it’s going better with you and hope for the best.

V/O 5 sec
Riana had visited the family in Kabul many times over the years,

Riana : Although we knew it was a dangerous place it was really safe in Kabul, we went for walks in the evening with the dogs, it was safe.

V/O 15 sec
But the recent Afghan elections and the gradual withdrawal of the international armies are a testing time. Terrorism is on the increase with the Taliban reasserting themselves. Now the big question is will the Afghan troops be able to control the territory.

V/O 4 sec
What happened last Saturday evening looks like one such example.

Devi: There have been so many stories …What happened Riana
Riana: This is what happened, Hannelie went to the hospital on Saturday morning they called her out for an emergency just before 1.30 2 Afghan people jumped over the wall

V/O 8 sec
The two men then killed the security guards and opened the gate into the compound letting in the rest of the group

Riaan: They entered the house and apparently went down to the basement a lot of people was in the basement, Werner was busy with a lecture when they entered the room Werner tried to protect the Afghan people and he jumped up.

Link
The gun men shot Werner first ,,,before running upstairs to where Jean Pierre and Rode were studying in their bed room.

Riana So they basically killed the two kids in Jean Pierre room.

Riana: and then they went back downstairs and they kept the people hostage in the basement and said they were waiting for the police because they said they want a war
Devi They want a war?
Riana: They want a war.

29th November Groenewald House Kabul Actual Footage

V/O 16 sec
About an hour later the police arrived, a suicide bomber activated his bomb, and set the house ablaze….. then a fire fight ensued between the terrorists and local Afghan forces. Two locals died in the confrontation.

Riana: The whole house burnt down except Jean Pierre’s room where the two kids bodies were in, luckily for Hannelie they could recover the two bodies.
Devi: Does anybody know why this happened because it sounds senseless to me?
Riana: Hannelie said to me she doesn’t understand, she cant believe it herself when I spoke to her last night she said I cant make sense of this whole story.

V/O 6 sec
Anneli Botha is a terrorism expert. She’s with the Institute for Security Studies.

Anneli Botha
Institute for Security Studies

Devi: Are these Random attacks or are they targeted?
Anneli: I would expect them to be targeted especially since they are Western it means the Taliban had to have intelligence within Kabul to identify where these people are, where do they stay, what is the normal working day like and to attack at the right moment.

V/O 10 sec
In the 10 days before Werner, Jean Pierre and Rode were murdered, there were three other attacks on foreigners in Kabul.

Devi: Why foreigners?
Anneli: Foreigners, are an excellent target. If you can kill a westerner then you are sure of attracting a lot of attention.
Devi: It’s as simple as that?
Anneli: Simple as that. Keep in mind that terrorism or violence is a way of communicating so the easiest way and the most dramatic way I can get that attention the org will use to their advantage.

Link
The Taliban immediately claimed responsibility for these killings…saying that Werner was had been trying to convert Moslems too Christianity.

Riana: Werner did not do Christian work in Afghanistan. I just want to set the record straight they went there to support and help the Afghans that was there mission and that was their work Yes they are Born again Christians they lived their life in their house as Christians.

V/O 7 sec
Before the family had moved to Afghanistan, Werner had been a pastor in the Morelete Park Church, with Dirkie.

Devi: How do you feel about the statement the Taliban later released saying it was all about Christianity?
Pastor: Werner wasn’t a missionary in that normal sense of the word, he went there because he was a relief worker a humanitarian worker he knows very well you cant go to those countries and do missionary work, he knew that,

V/O 3 and a half sec
But for the Taliban Anneli says that doesn’t really matter.

Anneli: They will try to find a reason justifying their actions Yes they were humanitarian workers but in their mind set by claiming that they were Chris mercenaries places an emphasis not only with own members but also to outside world that we have aright to defend our religion in this regard.

V/O 16 sec
South Africa doesn’t have an embassy in Afghanistan but the Department of International Relations and Co operation has been liaising with SA’s mission in Islamabad, Pakistan to do all they can to help Hannelie. Nelson Kgwete is their spokesman

Nelson Kgwete
Spokenman: DIRCO

Devi: The reality is though is you cant hold the government of Afghanistan responsible surely this is a militant wing within their borders.
Nelson: They are also engaged with a struggle to protect citizens from the Taliban and other armed groupings. We are talking here of unarmed civilians who are not engaged in any unlawful activity.

V/O 7 sec
Hannelie has lost not only her family but all her documents and priceless possessions were burnt in the house.

Nelson: We are in direct contact with her, we will make sure by the time she leaves Afghanistan the process of finalising the repatriation is concluded. Its our wish that she is not put in any harms way and she returns home alive but we are satisfied with the level of protection has been given to her.

V/O
Hannelie will be returning to South Africa hopefully within a week. With her will be the bodies of her children. Jean Pierre was 17 and Rhode had just celebrated her 15th birthday.

Riana: Now also with the funeral arrangements I’ve also asked Hannelie who should be the carriers of the coffins and she said but they don’t have friends, the kids don’t have friends in South Africa.
Devi: it just struck me in that moment were having this conversation and speaking in the present tense Im also thinking in the present tense but the minute you mention the coffins you thing, hang on a minute theres a funeral.
Riana Ya
Devi: How is your sister doing?
Hannelie at the moment is strong, she is emotional but she is strong, Im speaking to her every day about three times
Devi Not easy, I always think the strong people get it the hardest because people expect you to be strong
Riana: I think the reality is going to kick in when I see my sister.
